newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares led 2.05pct higher by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares led 2.05pct higher by blue chips.

text.p: Greek shares were driven above 1,600-points on Friday by a strong show in blue chip banks and industrials.

Brokers said the market's performance proved there was considerable underlying buying interest which was enlivened by news of strong half-year banking profits and a cut in the central bank's depo rates.

"Growing trading volume showed there was considerable buying interest at current price levels which longed for fresh impetus from the macroeconomy and the corporate sector," said Aris Simadis, broker at Interact Securities.
"We had renewed interest from both institutional and retail investors and I expect this to continue as long as the market is dealt with positive news."
National Bank and Alpha Credit Bank turned in large profit growth in their interim results announced late on Thursday.

Effective today, the Bank of Greece cut its basic and floor deposit facility rates by 30 basis points. It cited a large drop in interbank surplus liquidity and wider spreads between drachma and other EMS currency rates.
The one-month Athibor, Greece's reference interbank rate, dropped 34 basis points to 11.91 percent on Friday.

Interact's Simadis said investment strategy and goals had changed since the early months of 1997 and equities were not moved by expectations of sharply falling interest rates and CPI inflation anymore.
"There is a broad consensus that inflation and interest rates will show marginal improvement, if any, later this year, especially after the rally of the dollar," he said.
Hence, it is apparent that investors cannot rely on broader market moves but instead should pick blue chip banks and industrials with strong profit growth that will lead the index higher, he added.
The dollar extended a streak of record fixings against the drachma, climbing to 286.60 drachmas from Thursday's 285.75 at the Bank of Greece's fixing.
The Athens general index added 2.05 percent or 32.24 points to settle at 1,601.39 from Thursday's close.
